question.leadin: This province's sovereignty movement grew stronger during its "Quiet Revolution."
question.text: Name this largest Canadian province, the only majority French-speaking one.
question.clue: Following a crisis in this region, the War Measures Act was invoked by a Prime Minister who said "just watch me", Pierre Trudeau.

swap.text: This province is the most populous and borders both Minnesota and New York. The capital Ottawa and the major city of Toronto both lie in this province.
swap.clue: The First Nations leader Tecumseh was killed in this province during the Battle of the Thames (TIMS) in the War of 1812.

question.leadin: The sign language used by this group is considered severely endangered, with less than forty native speakers worldwide.
question.text: Name this ethnic group that is indigenous to the arctic regions of Greenland and North America. They are known for their use of kayaks and dog sleds in transportation and hunting.
question.clue: In the 1950s, this ethnic group's dogs were killed by the RCMP.

swap.leadin: Phrases like "sick animal," "trained seal," "evil genius," "does not have a spine," and "devoid of honour" are listed as unparliamentary language in a book titled for Arthur Beauchesne, a clerk of this body.
swap.text: Name this lower house of Canadian Parliament, which shares its name with the house in the UK contrasted with the House of Lords.
swap.clue: The ability of wealthy men to purchase housing and instill tenants willing to vote as they wished, along with the outsized representation possible in districts with a tiny number of residents, led to reform of this body in 1832.

question.leadin: During this man's tenure, his government created universal health care, as well as the Maple Leaf flag.
question.text: Name this Prime Minister who preceded Pierre Trudeau and won the nobel peace prize for his role in resolving the Suez Crisis.
question.clue: This successor to Louis St. Laurent as party leader accepted the Bomarc missile program and instituted universal healthcare.

swap.leadin: In 1959, a series of canals opened up in this river after a project funded by the Eisenhower administration.
swap.text: Name this river that originates in Lake Ontario before passing through Montreal and Quebec City.
swap.clue: After traversing this body of water, an explorer reached the village of Stadacona and kidnapped its chief Donnacona.

question.leadin: Answer the following about mass hysterias in history, none of which involve Pumpkin Spice Lattes.
question.text: In 1938, unsubstantiated reports of a "slasher" paralyzed a British town of this name. Another city of this name was leveled in 1917 by a massive ship explosion and provides Boston a Christmas tree every year as thanks for its subsequent aid.
question.clue: During the French and Indian War, the British army kept prisoners on Georges Island in this city's harbor.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a major North American oil exporter.
swap.text: Louis Riel led this mixed-race ethnic group in a failed rebellion against the Canadian government in 1885.
swap.clue: Garnet Wolseley led a namesake expedition to confront these people in 1870.

question.text: He organized resistance to the Manitoba Act, which transferred Metis-populated lands from the Hudson's Bay Company to the Canadian government. For 15 points, name this leader of the Northwest Rebellion, who was hanged in 1885 for such opposition activity.
question.clue: This man was captured with the Cree Chief Poundmaker during the Battle of Batoche, and he appointed a tribunal which sentenced Thomas Scott to death.

swap.text: Some Haudenosaunee believe "Iroquois" to be derived from the language of this tribe. This tribe fought the Haudenosaunee in the Beaver Wars and name a lake whose Manitoulin Island was sacred to the Anishinaabe.
swap.clue: Many of these people banded together with the related "Tobacco People," or Petun, after a 1648 attack that killed the Jesuit Jean de Brebeuf.

question.leadin: This man put down the Louis Riel led Red River Rebellion.
question.text: Name this first prime minister of Canada.
question.clue: One scandal that this man was involved in eventually cooled down because larger organizations in Great Britain and the United States took control of the project.

swap.leadin: This man cryptically replied "just watch me" when asked how far he would go to stop terrorism.
swap.text: Name this Prime Minister whose time in office saw the October Crisis and the passage of the Official Languages Act, which gave official recognition to both French and English.
swap.clue: When this leader was accused of mouthing profanity at opposition members, he claimed to have said "fuddle duddle," and he improved his nation's welfare system in the "Just Society" program.

question.text: This Frenchman explored the Gulf of St. Lawrence and the St. Lawrence rivers, and is credited with giving Canada its present name.
question.clue: On their second voyage, this person made contact with the residents of the village of Stadacona.

swap.leadin: Donald Smith drove this railway's last spike in Craigellachie, British Columbia.
swap.text: Name this transcontinental railway in Canada, completed in 1885.

question.leadin: The Canadian Bill of Rights, which was Canada's first federal law to protect human rights, was passed during the administration of this prime minister.
question.text: Name this prime minister of Canada who led the Progressive Conservative Party. This prime minister controversially cancelled the Avro Arrow program and accepted Bomarc missiles from the United States.
question.clue: He also cancelled the Avro Arrow program, halting production of fighter jets in his country, when he signed NORAD with the US. Raised in Saskatchewan, he passed his country's Bill of Rights, and presided over the opening of the St. Lawrence Seaway.

swap.leadin: Jean Chretien ("crate-YENN") led this party to a strong majority in the 1993 Canadian federal election.
swap.text: Name this centrist Canadian political party led from 1968 to 1984 by Pierre Trudeau.
swap.answerHtml: Liberal Party of Canada [or Parti libéral du Canada]
swap.clue: A request to dissolve parliament by a leader of this party was refused by Governor-General Julian Byng in 1926.

question.text: Some Arctic Small Tool traditions developed into phases of this culture, which notably lacked bow and drill technology. This culture preceded the Thule ("TOO-lee") culture.
question.answerHtml: Dorset culture [accept Early or Middle or Late Dorset]
question.clue: X-shaped incisions on figures' heads from this culture have been linked to shamanistic travels.

swap.leadin: This battle saw a stand by the Hunter Patriots under Nils von Schoultz.
swap.text: Identify this 1838 battle in which an army under Henry Dundas quashed a rebellion at a certain stronghold in Prescott.

question.text: Conrad Black gave up Canadian citizenship to take one of these things after a legal battle with Jean Chretien ("crate-YEN"). The Nickle Resolution bars Canadians from these things, which name a never-ratified amendment to the US Constitution and are banned in the first sentence of the Emoluments Clause.
question.answerHtml: titles of nobility [accept foreign peerages, knighthoods, baronetcies, orders, honors, decorations, or medals; accept Titles of Nobility Amendment or Canadian titles debate]

swap.text: This Canadian Prime Minister attended the joint funeral for nine of the women killed in the massacre. This man met with Ronald Reagan at the infamous "Shamrock Summit."
swap.clue: He replaced the Manufacturer's Tax with the Goods and Services Tax and passed an agreement that opponents like Ed Broadbent claimed would turn into the 51st state, the Free Trade Agreement.
